original_question: Show that the absolute complexity C(gamma(t)) of any L2 geodesic gamma(t) in D_mu^s(M) is bounded above by an exponential function of time and initial H^s speed.
target_in_paper: Problem 20 in Section 8.1 ("Complexity growth for 2D flows"): prove that for any geodesic γ(t) in D^s_μ(M), its absolute complexity satisfies C(γ(t)) ≲ e^(t||γ̇(0)||_{H^s}). ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core content of the paper’s Problem 20: the object C(γ(t)), the ambient space D^s_μ(M), the fact that γ(t) is an L^2 geodesic, and the intended exponential upper bound in terms of time and the initial H^s size. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
missing_details: The problem is posed only for a two-dimensional compact manifold M, possibly with boundary. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

D^s_μ(M) is the Sobolev H^s completion of the group D_μ(M) of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms, and the surrounding setup assumes s > n/2 + 1 so that the L^2 exponential map is smooth and locally invertible; in the 2D case this means s > 2. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The geodesics are geodesics of Arnold’s right-invariant L^2 kinetic-energy metric, not arbitrary paths in D^s_μ(M). ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
The paper defines U_ε by U_ε = exp_e(B_ε), where B_ε = {v in T_eD^s_μ(M) : ||v||_{H^s} < ε}. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

For η in D^s_μ(M), C_ε(η) is the minimal number of factors in a decomposition η = η_1 ◦ ... ◦ η_N with each η_i in U_ε. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
The absolute complexity is defined by C(η) = limsup_{ε->0} ε C_ε(η). ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The bound is stated in the sharper paper-faithful form C(γ(t)) ≲ e^(t||γ̇(0)||_{H^s}), not merely as some unspecified exponential function of time and initial speed. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

A stand-alone version should clarify that ||γ̇(0)||_{H^s} is the Sobolev norm of the initial tangent vector in the Sobolev/right-translated structure on TD^s_μ(M); the paper leaves this implicit. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
refined_question: Let M be a compact two-dimensional manifold, possibly with boundary, and let D^s_μ(M) be the Sobolev H^s completion (s > 2) of the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of M, equipped with Arnold’s right-invariant L^2 kinetic-energy metric. Let exp_e : T_eD^s_μ(M) -> D^s_μ(M) be the corresponding L^2 exponential map, and for ε > 0 define B_ε = {v in T_eD^s_μ(M) : ||v||_{H^s} < ε} and U_ε = exp_e(B_ε). For η in D^s_μ(M), let C_ε(η) be the minimal N such that η = η_1 ◦ ... ◦ η_N with each η_i in U_ε, and define the absolute complexity by C(η) = limsup_{ε->0} ε C_ε(η). Show that for every L^2 geodesic γ(t) in D^s_μ(M), one has C(γ(t)) ≲ e^(t||γ̇(0)||_{H^s}). ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 20 in Section 8.1, because that is the only official statement in the paper that introduces absolute complexity and asks for an exponential upper bound along geodesics. Section 8.1 provides the exact definitions of U_ε, C_ε, and C(η); Section 5.2 supplies the Sobolev completion D^s_μ(M), the hypothesis s > n/2 + 1, and the exponential map exp_e; and Section 1 identifies the relevant geodesics as those of the right-invariant L^2 metric on D_μ(M). The sentence after Problem 20 says this estimate would imply the standard double-exponential H^s bound for Euler solutions, but the paper does not state an equivalence, so the refined question should stay with Problem 20 itself. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
